units.title: Cell structure
points: Compare eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells and give examples of each
Label animal, plant and bacterial cells and state each organelle's function
Explain how adaptations of specialised cells suit their function
Calculate magnification, image and actual size using a light microscope
Describe aseptic technique in culturing microorganisms on agar plates
Interpret zone of inhibition results for antiseptics and antibiotics

units.title: Cell division
points: Describe the stages of mitosis and the cell cycle
Explain why mitosis is needed for growth, repair and asexual reproduction
Compare mitosis and binary fission in prokaryotes
Describe how stem cells can differentiate and where they are found
Discuss uses, risks and ethical issues of stem cell therapy

units.title: Culturing microorganisms
points: Describe how to prepare an uncontaminated culture of bacteria using agar plates
Explain why petri dishes and equipment are sterilised and why lids are taped
Calculate the number of bacteria in a population after a given time using mean division t…
Describe the effect of antiseptics and antibiotics on bacterial growth (required practica…

units.title: Transport in cells
points: Explain diffusion and state factors affecting the rate of diffusion
Describe osmosis and predict water movement from solute concentrations
Calculate percentage change in mass from the osmosis practical
Explain active transport and why it needs energy from respiration
Relate surface area to volume ratio to rates of exchange

units.title: Principles of organisation
points: Order cells, tissues, organs and organ systems in organisation
Relate the structure of a tissue to its function
Describe the role of enzymes as biological catalysts
Explain enzyme action using the lock-and-key model and specificity
Interpret enzyme rate graphs for temperature, pH and substrate concentration

units.title: Animal tissues, organs and organ systems
points: Describe the digestive system and the role of each digestive enzyme
Explain how the small intestine is adapted for absorption
Use qualitative reagents to test for sugars, starch, protein and lipids
Calculate and compare energy requirements from food data
Describe the heart, its blood vessels and the double circulatory system
Explain how the lungs, alveoli and blood vessels are adapted for exchange

units.title: Plant tissues, organs and systems
points: Identify the tissues in a leaf and state their functions
Explain how root hair cells and xylem absorb and move water and minerals
Describe transpiration and its rate affected by temperature, light, wind and humidity
Explain translocation in the phloem and the role of guard cells and stomata

units.title: Communicable diseases
points: Classify pathogens and describe methods of spreading disease
Describe symptoms, spread and control of named viral, bacterial, fungal and protist disea…
Explain how human defence systems prevent infection
Explain how vaccination produces immunity and protects populations
Compare antibiotics and painkillers and describe the problem of resistance
Describe the stages of drug discovery, testing and the role of trials

units.title: Monoclonal antibodies
points: Describe how monoclonal antibodies are produced from hybridomas
Explain their uses in diagnosis, pregnancy tests and cancer treatment
Evaluate the advantages and drawbacks of monoclonal antibody treatment

units.title: Plant disease
points: Describe symptoms of common plant diseases and their causes
Identify plant diseases from photographs and data
Explain physical and chemical plant defence responses
Explain how plant diseases are detected and controlled

units.title: Photosynthesis
points: State the word and balanced symbol equation for photosynthesis
Describe the effect of light intensity, carbon dioxide and temperature on the rate
Interpret limiting factor graphs and suggest improvements to the practical
Explain how leaf structure is adapted for efficient photosynthesis
Explain how plants use glucose and stored starch

units.title: Respiration
points: Write the word and balanced equation for aerobic respiration
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in muscles and yeast
Explain the effects of exercise and how the body responds to oxygen debt
Describe how metabolism uses the products of respiration

units.title: Sequences and series
points: Use arithmetic and geometric sequences and their nth terms
Find sums of finite arithmetic and geometric series
Find sums of infinite geometric series and conditions for convergence
Solve financial problems with compound interest and annuities
Use sigma notation and proof by induction on series

units.title: Exponents and logarithms
points: Apply laws of exponents and logarithms
Solve exponential and logarithmic equations
Use natural logarithms and base change
Sketch and analyse exponential and log graphs
Model growth and decay problems

units.title: Proof and number systems
points: Construct direct proofs and proofs by contradiction
Disprove statements with counterexamples
Use mathematical induction for formulas and divisibility
Apply the binomial theorem to expand and find terms
Count arrangements with permutations and combinations

units.title: Complex numbers and systems
points: Perform operations on complex numbers in Cartesian form
Use modulus-argument (polar) form and de Moivre's theorem
Find nth roots of complex numbers and sketch loci
Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions
Solve systems of linear equations with three unknowns

units.title: Functions and equations
points: Find domain, range, composite and inverse functions
Apply transformations and sketch modulus functions
Use factor and remainder theorems
Relate sums and products of roots to polynomial coefficients
Solve inequalities including rational and modulus inequalities

units.title: Geometry and trigonometry
points: Use reciprocal and inverse trigonometric functions
Apply compound and double angle identities
Solve trigonometric equations over a given interval
Use the unit circle, radians and symmetry properties
Solve 3D problems with sine and cosine rules

units.title: Vectors
points: Perform vector addition, scalar multiplication and dot product
Find equations of lines and planes
Determine angles between lines and planes
Find intersections and distances in 3D
Solve kinematics problems using vectors

units.title: Statistics and probability
points: Summarise data with central tendency and spread
Use correlation, regression and the coefficient of determination
Apply probability rules, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem
Work with discrete distributions and expectation algebra
Compute binomial and normal probabilities, including standardisation

units.title: Limits and differentiation
points: Evaluate limits, including L'Hôpital's rule
Differentiate from first principles
Apply chain, product and quotient rules
Differentiate with implicit differentiation and inverse trig functions
Discuss continuity and differentiability

units.title: Applications of calculus
points: Find tangents and normals and analyse curve behaviour
Use first and second derivatives for optimisation
Solve kinematics problems for displacement, velocity, acceleration
Sketch curves using derivatives and asymptotes
Model related rates and practical problems

units.title: Integration and differential equations
points: Integrate standard functions and by substitution
Use integration by parts and partial fractions
Evaluate definite integrals and find areas and volumes of revolution
Solve first-order differential equations by separation of variables
Solve linear differential equations with an integrating factor

units.title: Series and numerical methods
points: Find Maclaurin series for standard functions
Use series expansions to approximate values and limits
Test convergence and divergence of series
Apply Euler's method to approximate solutions
Combine series with limits and integration

syllabus.name: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind

units.title: An Animal of No Significance
points: Trace the timeline from 2.5 million years ago to the Cognitive Revolution
Explain why the brain and tool use set early hominins apart
Distinguish Homo sapiens from Neanderthals and other human species
Discuss the role of fire and cooking in early development

units.title: The Tree of Knowledge
points: Define the Cognitive Revolution as a leap in language and imagination
Explain gossip and how it binds social groups up to about 150 people
Describe how fiction enables large-scale cooperation
Contrast biological evolution with cultural evolution

units.title: A Day in the Life of the Sapiens
points: Reconstruct hunter-gatherer diet, work patterns and social life
Outline the foraging band and the 'ancient commune' debate
Explain how foragers shaped ecosystems through fire and hunting

units.title: Great Flood and the Agricultural
points: Describe the spread of Sapiens across continents and the extinctions that followed
Explain the Agricultural Revolution's timing and locations
Evaluate the 'luxury trap' argument on farming and human wellbeing
Contrast the sedentary farmer with the forager lifestyle

units.title: Building Pyramids
points: Explain imagined orders and how they become embedded in matter
Apply the story of Peugeot and the Declaration of Independence
Distinguish objective, subjective and intersubjective reality
Describe how large-scale cooperation depends on shared myths

units.title: The Unification of Humankind
points: Trace how empires, money and religion dissolve cultural boundaries
Explain money as the most universal system of mutual trust
Compare polytheism, monotheism and dualism, and humanist views
Explain how trade and conquest created a single human world

units.title: The Scientific Revolution
points: Explain why Europeans acknowledged ignorance and sought new knowledge
Describe feedback loops between science, empire and capitalism
Explain the rise of credit and the trust that underpins finance
Outline the voyages of discovery and the rise of the Atlantic empires

units.title: Industrial Revolution
points: Describe the shift from agrarian to industrial production and energy sources
Explain capitalism, credit and the role of private profit in growth
Explain how imperialism supplied raw materials and markets
Give the link between consumption, consumerism and growth

units.title: The Idea of Man and the End of Empires
points: Trace how nationalism, culture and the state reordered society
Explain how empires fell and nation-states replaced them
Discuss how capitalism, science and empire were intertwined
Explain how war and totalitarianism reshaped modern polities

units.title: Reunification of Humankind
points: Evaluate policy options for the future: war, ecology and technology
Discuss the promise and risk of biotechnology and artificial intelligence
Evaluate humanism versus dataism in the book's conclusion
Reflect on whether Sapiens will survive as a species

units.title: Happy Few and the Mystery of Happiness
points: Compare biological, psychological and philosophical accounts of happiness
Relate happiness to evolution's expectations
Evaluate the verdicts on modern life and meaning
Discuss how history informs ideas of a better future

units.title: Electrostatics
points: State and apply Gauss's law to find field of a charge distribution
Define electric potential as work done per unit charge
Relate electric field and potential gradient
Derive and use energy stored in a capacitor
Describe charging and discharging of a capacitor
Explain electric polarization of dielectrics

units.title: Current Electricity
points: Apply Kirchhoff's first and second laws to circuits
Solve series and parallel network problems
Calculate power and energy dissipated in resistors
Use the potentiometer and Wheatstone bridge principles
Explain internal resistance and EMF of a cell

units.title: Electromagnetism
points: Define magnetic flux density and use F = BIL sinθ
Find field due to current in a straight wire and a solenoid
Calculate torque on a current-carrying loop
Explain the working of a galvanometer and ammeter
Describe magnetic properties of materials

units.title: Electromagnetic Induction
points: State and apply Faraday's law of induction
Use Lenz's law to find direction of induced current
Explain self and mutual inductance
Describe the AC and DC generator
Explain the principle of a transformer

units.title: Alternating Current
points: Describe AC through resistor, inductor and capacitor
Calculate reactance and impedance
Explain resonance and compute resonant frequency
Find power and power factor in AC circuits
Describe the components and working of an AC generator

units.title: Physics of Solids
points: Explain energy bands in conductors, insulators and semiconductors
Describe intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors
Explain p-n junction and diode characteristics
Describe uses of LED, photodiode and solar cell
Explain transistor action and its applications

units.title: Electronics
points: Explain the operation of a transistor amplifier
Use operational amplifier basics
Analyse logic gates and truth tables
Explain digital electronics and number systems
Describe applications of logic circuits

units.title: Dawn of Modern Physics
points: Explain the photoelectric effect and Einstein's equation
Describe wave-particle duality and de Broglie wavelength
Outline relativistic mass, length and time effects
Explain the Compton effect
Describe the uncertainty principle

units.title: Atomic Spectra
points: Explain Bohr's model and energy levels
Describe spectral series of hydrogen
Calculate photon energy for transitions
Distinguish emission and absorption spectra
Explain the laser principle

units.title: Nuclear Physics
points: Describe radioactive decay with half-life calculations
Explain nuclear fission and fusion processes
Calculate mass defect and binding energy
Describe basic forces of nature
Explain uses and hazards of radioactivity

critics: realism 100: Every day is within what you usually sustain.
exam_prep 50: fewer than two spaced retrieval sessions; no light review on Tue 26 Jan
front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.
